dataset.description: Methodologically, it employs a mixed-methods approach that combines quantitative analyses of emission data and energy consumption with qualitative insights through stakeholder interviews. This robust methodology allows for a comprehensive understanding of the measurable impacts of implemented policies and nuanced perspectives of various stakeholders. This approach enhances the depth and breadth of the research and sets a precedent for future studies in similar settings, advocating for an integrative methodological framework that can capture the multifaceted nature of airport ecosystems. Using multiple data source, triangulating data by collecting information from multiple sources – emission data from airport records, energy consumption data from utility bills, qualitative insights from stakeholder interviews, allows for cross-validation, reliability, and a more comprehensive understanding. Substantively, it contributes significantly to the field of sustainable aviation by developing actionable, evidence-based policy recommendations and a sustainable business framework that can be implemented at RIX airport and potentially at other international airports. These contributions are poised to directly impact the operational and environmental performance of airports, demonstrating how integrated approaches can achieve substantial reductions in carbon emissions and improvements in energy efficiency. Moreover, by fostering a culture of inclusivity and engagement, RIXopolis substantively contributes to the socio-political aspects of airport management, potentially reshaping how stakeholders are involved in the decision-making processes at airports globally.

distribution.title: The purpose of data collection and generation in the RIXopolis project is to develop an evidence-driven framework that facilitates the transformation of Riga International Airport (RIX) into a climate-neutral, efficient, and politically inclusive ecosystem.

dmp.description:
RIXopolis adopts an evidence-driven, interdisciplinary approach that integrates state-of-the-art policy frameworks, business innovations, and sustainable practices to address pressing challenges in airport ecosystems. Leveraging the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) and Institutional Theory, the project focuses on:
Reducing carbon emissions and optimizing energy consumption.
Fostering a politically inclusive culture that engages diverse stakeholders.
Applying smart energy and mobility solutions for sustainability.
The research employs a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative analyses of emissions and energy usage with qualitative stakeholder interviews to holistically understand the socio-economic and environmental impacts of proposed policy innovations.
